category_title: Medium-proficiency students who struggle with run-on sentences and L1/L2 translation issues
minimal_context: The student is logging into the Blackboard learning system to write a reflective journal post and leave comments for their mixed-proficiency peer group.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please log into Blackboard and write your peer comment for your group members, then complete your own journal reflection about the assignment.

STUDENT: I will post my comment to my group member first. I wrote: 'As an international student, I understand that writing is hard, especially with second language. I understand how hard to organize thoughts and choose the correct words. I ’m from Korea. In Kore a, it is more important to write in correct grammar too. They don't teach how to organize thoughts and write an essay.'

TUTOR: Thank you for sharing that with your group. Now, please write your own journal reflection about your experience with the assignment.

STUDENT: I will write about the good things first. The good thing is that I felt tha t writing is interesting. I don’ t have perfect grammar skills or writing skills, but when I wrote about personal narrative assignment, I felt that writing was fun. I just need to practice more on grammer and use of English language.

TUTOR: Okay, please continue your reflection. What else do you want to add about your experience?

STUDENT: I will add the bad things. Because of the problems with use of English language, I lost confidence in writing. Writing was very hard as I imagined. Since I am not a good talker, I had troubles with expressing my thoughts in a proper way. This was all bad thing during this assignment.

options.A: Implement relatively tight timelines for the completion of the Blackboard journal posts and peer comments.
options.B: Restrict viewership of the Blackboard journal posts to only class participants and the instructor.
options.C: Establish the working practices of the mixed-proficiency group via a consensus pledge and continually reinforce it.
options.D: Enable the use of autocorrect and text prediction functions within the Blackboard learning system.
